newsitem.title: UK: Poll fears deter U.S. utility predators-paper.
newsitem.headline: Poll fears deter U.S. utility predators-paper.

text.p: Fears that Britain's Labour Party will win the next general election and impose a windfall tax on the bumper profits reaped by Britain's privatised electricity firms are putting off U.S. utility predators, The Times said.

The newspaper said in its Monday edition that one large U.S. company was "said to have" pulled out of a hostile bid at the last moment after "taking fright at the campaign being waged against utilities by Labour" in the run-up to the election.
The Times quoted industry watchers as tipping Southern Electric, which has seen at least two plans to merge with other UK utilities foiled, as the possible target by the unnamed U.S. utility.
"American utilities are believed to have withdrawn from the race to buy British electricity companies..." The Times said.
The British general election has to be held by next May.
